title: Creating a project with name, description, category, budget, timeline, tags, and team members produces a fully-populated project
description: Covers CreateProjectModal end to end: the modal posts to POST /projects/:orgId with an Idempotency-Key header, then makes follow-up addProjectMember calls for each picked team member (project has no team field of its own on creation).
preconditions: Logged in as a user with project.create
At least 2 other org users exist to pick as team members
steps: Navigate to /project-management and click 'New Project'
Fill Project Name, Description, select Status=Planning, Priority=High, Category=Compliance
Set Allocated Budget=50000, Estimated Hours=200, Start Date and End Date, add tag 'iso27001'
In the Team Members section, add 2 users from the picker
Click 'Create Project'
expectedResult: Modal closes, the new project appears at the top of the project list with correct name/status/priority/budget badges and a Team avatar group showing 2 members; the project detail page shows both team members with the system 'Member' role.

title: Project dashboard stats cards reflect real aggregate data after creating and completing projects
description: GET /projects/:orgId/dashboard aggregates totalProjects/totalBudget and a per-status breakdown across only isActive:true projects the caller can see (resolveProjectIdsScope).
preconditions: Org has 3 active projects: 1 Planning, 1 Active with $10,000 budget, 1 Completed
steps: Navigate to /project-management as an org admin
Read the Total Projects, Total Budget, Active Projects, and Completed stats cards
expectedResult: Total Projects = 3, Total Budget = $10,000 (sum of budget.allocated across all 3, since only one has a non-zero budget), Active Projects = 1, Completed = 1 — all values match the underlying project records exactly, no stale caching.

title: Editing a project's fields persists and is immediately reflected on both the list and detail views
steps: Navigate to /project-management/[id]/edit
Change Status to 'Active', Priority to 'Critical', update the Description
Save changes
Navigate back to /project-management (list) and to /project-management/[id] (detail)
expectedResult: Both the list row and the detail page show status badge 'Active' (green) and priority badge 'Critical' (red) with the updated description — no manual page refresh required beyond normal client-side navigation, and the change is attributed to the editing user via updatedBy on the backend.

title: Switching the active project in ProjectSelector correctly re-scopes data shown in other modules
description: ProjectSelector dispatches setSelectedProject, updating state.projects.selectedProject app-wide. Other modules (evidence-management, risk-register, audit-assurance) read the selected project to filter their own project-scoped queries.
preconditions: User is a member of two distinct projects, Project A and Project B, each with its own evidence items and risks
steps: Select Project A in the Navbar's ProjectSelector
Navigate to Evidence Management and Risk Register, note the items shown
Switch the selector to Project B without logging out
Re-check Evidence Management and Risk Register
expectedResult: After switching to Project B, Evidence Management and Risk Register show only Project B's items — none of Project A's evidence/risks remain visible, and the switch takes effect without a full page reload being required.

title: Archiving a project soft-deletes it, hides it from the default list, and it can be restored
steps: From the project list, click the Archive icon on the project row and confirm the browser dialog
Verify the project disappears from the default (non-archived) list
Toggle 'Show Archived' on and locate the project
Click 'Restore' on the archived project
expectedResult: After archiving, PUT /projects/project/:id/archive sets isActive:false and the project vanishes from the default view but appears under Show Archived with a Restore action. After restoring, PUT /projects/project/:id/restore sets isActive:true and the project reappears in the default list with all its original field data intact (data retention — nothing was actually deleted).

title: 'Delete Project' only soft-deletes despite the confirmation dialog stating the project will be permanently removed
description: The frontend AlertDialog text reads 'This action cannot be undone. The project will be permanently removed,' but DELETE /projects/project/:id (exports.remove, project.controller.js) executes `Project.findByIdAndUpdate(req.params.id, { isActive: false })` and responds with message 'Project archived' — functionally identical to the Archive action, not a hard delete. This is a real UX/messaging mismatch worth flagging: data is fully recoverable server-side even though the UI promises otherwise.
preconditions: An active project, plus direct DB/API access to verify post-state
steps: From the project list (with Show Archived off), click the Archive icon to move a project into the archived view
With Show Archived on, click the Trash/Delete icon on the archived project and confirm 'Delete' in the AlertDialog
Independently query the project by ID via GET /projects/project/:id as an org admin (or inspect the database record) immediately after
expectedResult: Actual current behavior: the project disappears from the client's local list state (removed via setProjects filter) but the underlying document still exists in MongoDB with isActive:false — GET /projects/project/:id still returns the full record, and the response body is a plain success/'Project archived' message, not the promised permanent removal. Flag for product/eng: either implement true irreversible deletion or correct the dialog copy to match soft-delete/data-retention reality.

title: Retrying project creation after a simulated network timeout does not create a duplicate project
description: CreateProjectModal generates a client-side creationRequestId (crypto.randomUUID) once per submission attempt and sends it as the Idempotency-Key header; a retry with the same key resolves to the original project via findIdempotentProject rather than creating a second one.
preconditions: Ability to simulate a network interruption (e.g. throttle/kill the connection) right after the POST is sent but before the response returns
steps: Open Create Project modal, fill in a project name, and submit while simulating a dropped connection so the client never receives the response
Observe the 'connection was interrupted... Retry safely' error message
Click Create Project again without closing the modal (same creationRequestIdRef is reused)
expectedResult: The retry returns HTTP 200 with idempotentReplay:true and the SAME project _id as the original attempt; exactly one project document exists for this name/org, confirmed by checking the project list shows only a single entry.

title: A user with memberships in two projects cannot see the other project's team roster or data through either project's context
preconditions: User is a plain Member of Project A only (no membership in Project B)
Project B exists in the same org with a different team
steps: Log in as the user and open ProjectSelector — confirm only Project A is listed
Attempt to directly navigate to /project-management/[Project-B-id] by URL
Attempt GET /api/projects/project/:ProjectB_id/team via browser devtools/API client using the logged-in session
expectedResult: ProjectSelector lists only Project A. Direct navigation to Project B's detail page shows an error/access-denied state (backend returns 403). The team roster call for Project B also returns 403 — no cross-project data leakage through any of the three access paths.
